title: RAYE Announces One-Night Orchestral Show at Royal Albert Hall
excerpt: RAYE has announced a one-night orchestral concert at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23, where she will perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full.
body:
RAYE has announced a one-night orchestral concert at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23, where she will perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full. The show, titled *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, will bring her band together with the Heritage Orchestra and Flames Collective choir. It is the same musical partnership behind her much-discussed symphonic performances of *My 21st Century Blues*, but the repertoire will be completely new. This time, RAYE is bringing an album that already contains orchestral music, big-band arrangements and songs written to follow one another across a longer story.

The venue was the setting for her first large-scale symphonic concert in 2023. Backed by a 50-piece orchestra and choir, she performed songs from *My 21st Century Blues* in a show later released as *Live at the Royal Albert Hall*. The film was subsequently nominated for Best Music Film at the Grammy Awards. A sold-out performance at London's O2 in 2024 brought the orchestra and choir back together, demonstrating that the arrangement was more than an experiment for a single night. The new concert returns to the Hall three years after the original performance, with an entirely different collection of songs to arrange.

Released in March, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* was conceived in four sections that RAYE calls seasons. It begins in a troubled place and moves through different styles and emotions toward a hopeful conclusion. The musical changes are just as pronounced. There is jazz and soul alongside cinematic orchestration, including "Click Clack Symphony.", a collaboration with Hans Zimmer. Elsewhere, intimate vocals give way to full-band performances, and the songs occasionally shift direction within the same track. For the Royal Albert Hall concert, those contrasts will be heard with a dedicated orchestra and choir rather than the changing instrumentation of the studio recordings.

RAYE has released a new version of "I Will Overcome." to accompany the concert announcement. Filmed at Abbey Road Studios, it features the London Symphony Orchestra rather than the Heritage Orchestra booked for the October show. The song comes directly after the album's brief introduction, giving listeners an early indication of its themes of endurance and recovery. The new performance is a separate recording, not footage from the Royal Albert Hall concert, and RAYE has not announced a concert film or live album for the upcoming date. The Abbey Road video is the first confirmed opportunity to hear one of these songs in a newly arranged symphonic performance.

[youtube:Iy2FoVeIUXs]

The announcement follows a busy year onstage. RAYE played six sold-out concerts at the O2 during her arena tour and subsequently appeared as a guest on Bruno Mars' North American stadium dates. She also performed "I Will Overcome." at September's MTV Video Music Awards. Those appearances put the newer material in front of large audiences, but the Royal Albert Hall show will focus on the complete album rather than songs selected from across her career. The record became her first UK No. 1 album, while "WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!" passed a billion Spotify streams. Both successes have happened alongside her increasing use of orchestras in live performances.

The album has a different sort of ending from its most exuberant single. After "WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!" come songs involving RAYE's family, including "Joy." with her sisters Amma and Absolutely, before the six-minute closing track "Fin.". There, she speaks to the listener who has stayed with the record until its final song, offering thanks rather than another large pop chorus. The concert announcement promises the album in full, although it does not specify the running order or any additional songs. Whatever else is included on the night, that quieter farewell is part of the music RAYE has chosen to bring back to the Hall.
